pages.text: "Ow!" Nils the little bear pulled back his paw while gathering firewood. A black dot had stuck in his paw pad: a wooden splinter. It stung whenever he pressed it.
Grandpa Bruno held out his broad palm. "Nils, let me see your paw." "N-no! It does not hurt at all!" Nils tucked his paw behind his back.

It stung when he put wood in the stove, and when he picked up bread. Nils pressed the hurt paw against his tummy and used only the other one. "Taking it out would hurt even more..." The thought made him shrink back.
Grandpa sat in the chair by the stove. "Do you know what a splinter is? A tiny piece of wood that came off the firewood." "...A piece of wood?" Nils looked up.
"That little piece got lost inside your paw. It cannot find the door out." Grandpa adjusted his round glasses. "If we open the door, it can slip right out."
"Will it hurt?" Nils asked. "One little sting, as quick as a blink. Splinter out—all done!" Nils swallowed and held out his paw just a little.
Nils placed his paw on Grandpa's palm and repeated three steps. "One, open your paw wide! Two, phew—take a big breath!" "Three, watch the stove fire!" Nils turned his eyes toward the stove.
Grandpa touched it with the tip of his claw. "Splinter out—all done!" "...Oh? Already?" Nils blinked. One black piece of wood lay on Grandpa's palm.
Grandpa dipped Nils's paw in warm water. Even pressing it no longer stung. "It does not hurt! Not at all!" Nils raised both paws.
Nils used that paw to gather and carry firewood. Grandpa hugged him close. Show where it hurts instead of hiding it, so it can get better. "Grandpa, splinter out—all done!" Nils smiled.
